summary:
Our team worked together to develop a Mars exploration map designed to help astronauts navigate the planet more safely and efficiently. We started by researching the challenges of exploring Mars and identifying the factors that could affect astronauts during their missions, such as terrain, soil conditions, temperature, radiation, and potential hazards.

After discussing different ideas, we decided to create an interactive map that combines important environmental information with navigation routes. We focused on making the concept practical and easy to understand, while also thinking about how it could be improved in the future.

Throughout the project, we shared ideas, divided tasks, researched information, and worked on the design and presentation. Despite the limited time and challenges we faced, we managed to bring our idea together and submit our project before the deadline.
details:
Project Overview & How It Works

Astrolabe (أسطرلاب) is a bilingual (Arabic/English) tactical navigation and mission-planning web application built for astronauts conducting Extravehicular Activities (EVAs) on Mars. Centered on Jezero Crater's Western Delta (18.33062^\circ\text{ N}, 77.63036^\circ\text{ E}) and extending westward through Neretva Vallis and the Western Crater Rim into Nili Planum, it connects regional orbital mapping with micro-scale human surface mobility.

By fusing four NASA datasets—HiRISE DEM/MOLA (topography & slope), HiRISE Optical (aerial terrain), SHARAD/CRISM (subsurface water ice & mineralogy), and THEMIS IR (thermal inertia)—Astrolabe runs a Human-Optimal Weighted A* pathfinding engine. Clicking any destination computes the safest route from the fixed Astrolabe Base while avoiding slopes >15^\circ and loose sand ripples, showing a real-time Route Safety Score (%) alongside dual foot-walkback and rover-assisted safety perimeters.

Key Features, Benefits & Intended Impact

Astrolabe improves astronaut safety, mission efficiency, and scientific discovery during surface traverses through:

Bullet Astronaut Helmet Visor HUD: Displays live biometric telemetry (heart rate, \text{O}_2 reserve, suit battery, core temperature, and radiation dose).

Bullet Solar Storm Emergency Reroute: One-click rerouting toward natural terrain shielding.

Bullet Resource & Mineral Identification: Scientific classification of key targets (\text{H}_2\text{O} Ice, \text{CaSO}_4\cdot n\text{H}_2\text{O}, \text{Fe/Mg}-Smectites, \text{MgCO}_3/\text{FeCO}_3, \text{SiO}_2\cdot n\text{H}_2\text{O}, and \txt{FeO})

Bullet Field Logging: An interactive "+ Add Discovery" tool for recording observations in the field.

Creativity, Tools & Considered Factors

What makes Astrolabe distinct is how it translates multi-source orbital data into practical, human-centered EVA decision support—combining slope/terrain constraints, walkback/rover safety envelopes, biometric awareness, and emergency shielding in a single HUD workflow. In designing the system, our team prioritized astronaut survivability, terrain traversability, bilingual accessibility (Arabic/English), and clear integration of NASA planetary datasets into an interactive web interface
